subject: Gila monster
title: A Venomous Lizard's Spit Started the Ozempic Drug Family

scenes.text: One of the world's best-selling drug families started with a venomous lizard.
The Gila monster can go months without eating, and its blood sugar stays steady.
In the early 1990s, Dr. John Eng at a Bronx veterans hospital found a hormone in its venom.
It mimics human GLP-1, which tells your body to release insulin. But ours breaks down in about two minutes.
The lizard's version lasted for hours. In 2005, it became exenatide, the first drug of its kind.
Ozempic came later, a modified human version. But the whole family started with this lizard.

description:
The GLP-1 drug family, which now includes Ozempic, began with the venom of the Gila monster.
In the early 1990s, Dr. John Eng at the Bronx VA Medical Center isolated exendin-4 from Gila monster venom. It acts like human GLP-1, which prompts insulin release, but lasts for hours instead of breaking down in about two minutes. Its synthetic form, exenatide (Byetta), was approved by the FDA in 2005. Semaglutide (Ozempic) is a later, modified human GLP-1, no longer derived from the venom.
Which animal do you think will inspire the next big medicine?
first_comment: Fun detail: the VA declined to patent the discovery. Which animal do you think holds the next big medicine?
